author: harness:claude-code

patch.value: The gate contributors run before merging fails on every Claude Code workstation and passes on the runner for the same tree, because a harness probe writes advisory warnings into the surface the token budget measures

pnpm quality:static runs pnpm quality:token-budget, which measures pm health --check-only inside a sandboxed fixture and compares it to a committed baseline of 152 tokens / 604 bytes. On this workstation the measured output is 267 tokens / 1066 bytes and the gate blocks. On the hosted runner the same tree passes; CI run 31938652077 on main reports Gates (static) success. The difference is two advisory health warnings, provenance_resolver_zero_success:claude-code:model:claude_session_file:12 and the matching version row, emitted because the host process is a Claude Code session and the claude_session_file resolver is attempted once per fixture item inside a sandbox that has no session file. The gate already sets PM_AUTHOR explicitly, which does not suppress harness probing.

The token-budget gate's measured surfaces do not vary with the harness running the suite, proven by a control that sets each supported harness's signal environment and asserts the verdict is unchanged; A resolver that cannot succeed in a sandbox because the sandbox has no session artifact does not raise a per-item advisory warning into a measured surface, or health's measured projection excludes advisory findings and the exclusion is declared; The local and hosted invocation of quality:token-budget produce the same verdict for the same tree, asserted rather than observed; The neutralization covers every harness signal the detector reads, not only the ambiguous foreign one, closing the gap between pm-xgah3a's first acceptance criterion and what its fix delivered
A contributor running the mandated pre-merge gate on a clean checkout of main gets the same verdict CI gets.
The gate blocks on any Claude Code workstation and passes in CI, for a reason unrelated to token budgets.

message: Filed after reproducing the divergence with and without the harness signal environment on identical fixtures

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Reproduction, identical fixture built twice at tree 9da5886cc with dist built from it.

Setup in both runs (mirrors scripts/release/token-budget-gate.mjs runCli): isolated PM_PATH and PM_GLOBAL_PATH, PM_NO_TELEMETRY=1, PM_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1, PM_TELEMETRY_OTEL_DISABLED=1, PM_TELEMETRY_PROMPT=0, PM_AUTHOR=token-budget-gate; then init --defaults, install audit --project, then 12 create calls.

  Run A, host environment inherited (a Claude Code session):
    pm health --check-only  ->  1,066 bytes
    warnings: provenance_resolver_zero_success:claude-code:model:claude_session_file:12
              provenance_resolver_zero_success:claude-code:version:claude_session_file:12
    findings severity: advisory, check: storage

  Run B, identical except the harness signal variables are unset
  (CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT, CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION,
   CLAUDE_CODE_BRIDGE_SESSION_ID, CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH, CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET,
   CLAUDE_PID, CLAUDE_EFFORT, AI_AGENT):
    pm health --check-only  ->  594 bytes
    provenance_resolver_zero_success occurrences: 0

Committed baseline in scripts/release/token-budgets.json for health-default: baseline_bytes 549, baseline_estimated_tokens 138, max_bytes 604, max_estimated_tokens 152. Run B fits; run A does not.

Independence from this session's changes: git stash push -u followed by the gate on the resulting clean tree reproduces the same failure, so it is not caused by the working-tree diff.

Trailing count 12 equals the number of items created, so the resolver is attempted once per mutation rather than once per session. The gate's own PM_AUTHOR override does not suppress the probe.

Why this is a recurrence rather than a new class: pm-xgah3a's first acceptance criterion required a sandboxed workspace to neutralize the harness signal environment so recorded provenance never depends on the process running the suite, and its resolution states it hardened sandboxes against only the ambiguous foreign AI_AGENT signal. pm-t7wn04's first two criteria required the token-budget gate's measured surfaces to be independent of ambient host state and required a negative control proving the same verdict on a runner and on a workstation for the same tree. Both are closed; both properties fail here today.

value.note: runCli spreads process.env into the sandboxed fixture,so host harness signals reach the measured command
health-default baseline that the harness-dependent warnings exceed
